title: Uniparts India: management promise-vs-delivery ledger and credibility score (FY25 Q1 - FY27 Q2)
body: Pilot of the promise tracker. 10 concalls (2024-08-09 to 2026-11-05) gave 68 forward-looking promises, scored against later calls and screener.in quarterly numbers as of 2026-11-19. Of 47 resolved: 26 delivered, 7 partly, 6 missed, 6 moved-goalpost, 2 silently-dropped; 21 pending. Hit rate 55%. Management Credibility Score (MCS; scale -1.5..+1, weight = specificity x materiality x 8-quarter half-life) = +0.28 overall. Two very different regimes: FY25 calls (promoter Paramjit Soni guiding into a downturn) MCS -0.24, hit rate 33%. FY25 revenue was guided flat to -3% and came in at -15%; 'Q4 highest quarter' was restated, and the restatement was then denied. FY26-27 calls (COO, later CEO, Tanushree Bagrodia) MCS +0.65, hit rate 78%. Mid-teens FY26 guide vs +21% actual; FY27 raised three times. The split that matters is cycle vs execution, not the person: cycle/financial promises MCS +0.53, execution/strategic promises (Mexico, acquisition/third platform, fabrication, aftermarket) MCS -0.08. Mexico slipped about 10 months, with every new date called 'on track'. The acquisition promised 'within the next year or so' (Nov-2024) never happened; two deals fell through. Aftermarket was guided mid-teens, then single digit, and actually fell ~9% in FY26. Candour index ~5%: only 1 of 21 shortfalls was admitted unprompted (Hurricane Helene). Explanations came only when analysts asked. Tone vs delivery: upbeat tone with near-term misses in FY25. In FY26-27 numeric guides were conservative and beaten, but execution items kept an 'on track' tone while they slipped. Volunteered promises scored worse (MCS -0.29) than prompted ones (+0.43). Read: trust the revenue/margin guide in an upturn as a floor; discount strategic and timeline promises by ~1-3 quarters and the acquisition story heavily. Caveats: one scorer, no second-pass review; era is confounded with the cycle; segment data is mostly management-only.

data.tone_delivery_gap: FY25: high optimism, poor near-term delivery (gap large). FY26-27: measured tone, numeric beats (gap small/negative); execution items: persistent 'on track' language while slipping (gap large).
